future_native_option.reason: Packed and Morton integer encodings may behave differently in native C++ where Python object and function-call overhead is absent.
future_native_option.rule: Do not delay the MAF-3D inference prototype for native address optimization unless addressing becomes a measured runtime bottleneck.

next_research_step: Build a deterministic neutral MAF-3D representation hierarchy using tuple-based MAF addressing, then test route-conditioned hidden-state reconstruction against the untouched Qwen oracle.
not_supported: Morton encoding is universally slower across languages or native implementations.
Packed integer addressing can never outperform tuple addressing in native code.
The Python shallow-size estimate is an end-to-end memory measurement.
This benchmark measures hidden-state inference quality.
This benchmark proves or disproves MAF as an LLM replacement.
supported_conclusions: Under the frozen Python MAF-3D address benchmark, tuple-based flat addressing was the fastest candidate on the preregistered primary address-plus-lookup metric at one million entries.
Packed integer keys improved lookup-only latency and reduced estimated shallow Python bytes per entry, but their encoding overhead made end-to-end address-plus-lookup slower than tuple addressing.
Morton3D reduced estimated shallow Python bytes per entry but was slower than tuple addressing on both the primary metric and the five-step hierarchy traversal.
MAF-3D V1 should therefore retain tuple-based addressing and focus fractal research above the physical address layer on route-conditioned representation and traversal.
